1. Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp spikes — reduce initial forecast by 5–10% if recent history shows volatility.

2. Model underestimates prices during prolonged downward trends — increase forecast by 3–7% if 7+ days of declining prices precede the forecast window.

3. Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, adjust downward by 1–3% unless confirmed by macro signals.

4. Forecast lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days — if true outcome is rising, model often peaks 1–2 days later; adjust forecast to align with 1-day lagged true value.

5. Overshoot after spikes — if model forecasts >15% above recent peak, reduce by 10–20% to avoid overcorrection.

6. Model underestimates price volatility in high-activity months — increase forecast variance by 2–5% if historical volatility >1.5σ in prior 30 days.

7. Avoid overfitting to recent 30-day history — if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 5–10% to prevent momentum bias.
